items.title: Live: Netanyahu says Trump knows 'exactly what he's doing' as oil prices rise after US ultimatum
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Donald Trump knows "exactly what he's doing" when he is asked about the US president's threats to strike Iran's power plants if the Strait of Hormuz is not opened. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Bowen confirms petrol stations on east coast experiencing shortages
items.description: Energy Minister Chris Bowen has confirmed dozens of petrol stations on Australia's east coast are facing shortages amid a Question Time grilling on fuel supplies. Follow live.

items.title: World energy watchdog warns fuel crisis is 'very severe'
items.description: World leaders have failed to grasp the depth of the energy crisis created by the Iran war, the head of the International Energy Agency has warned, as he considers releasing extra emergency oil stores.

items.title: As One Nation's vote soars, SA supporters explain their reasons
items.description: Heading into the South Australian election, One Nation was backing its chances to pick up votes from across the political spectrum, and supporters say various factors informed their decisions.

items.title: Nine seats to watch as counting continues after the SA election
items.description: ABC chief elections and data analyst Casey Briggs looks at what seats are still in doubt in the South Australian state election, as One Nation makes it into the final two candidates in the count in most of the state's 47 electorates.

items.title: Ambulances set on fire in suspected antisemitic hate crime in London
items.description: Footage posted on social media appears to show three hooded people pouring gasoline on the vehicles before leaving the scene.

items.title: Live: ASX down after another brutal night on Wall Street, oil keeps rising
items.description: Despite clawing back some of its earlier losses, the ASX 200 has started the new week in negative territory after a fall on Wall Street as oil prices continue to rise. Follow the day's events from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Work-from-home mandates unlikely as NSW grapples with fuel price hike
items.description: Commuters are turning to public transport in droves amid skyrocketing fuel prices, but the NSW government has stopped short of implementing reduced or free fares in response.

items.title: Ex-Cyclone Narelle expected to possibly curve back to WA coast this week
items.description: Strong winds and heavy rain are expected as ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle crosses the border from the Northern Territory into Western Australia.

items.title: ABC staff to go on 24-hour strike after rejecting pay offer
items.description: Staff were informed this morning that a majority of ABC workers had voted against the broadcaster's latest enterprise agreement offer.

items.title: Man who killed Nikkita Azzopardi found dead in Melbourne jail cell
items.description: A killer who fatally bashed his partner in her home has been found dead in a Melbourne prison, ahead of his transfer to a secure mental health facility.

items.title: A horrific accident cost Ghanim his arms, but delivered an unexpected twist
items.description: Ghanim Al Shnen became a pioneer in the use of mind-controlled robotic limbs after losing both his arms. Although he would never have chosen this fate, it ultimately gave him the life for which he longed.

items.title: Markets want to believe all will be OK as Iran war threatens global economy
items.description: The markets' benign assessment of the Iran war is wrong and the damage to the global economy could get worse.

items.title: BYO sandwiches and no cafe lunches as retirements threatened by rising costs
items.description: The Australian retirement dream is being destabilised by the rising cost of home insurance, as retirees on fixed budgets find themselves unable to absorb skyrocketing premiums.

items.title: Have an easier morning thanks to these make-ahead breakfast recipes
items.description: From breakfast sandwiches to chia pudding, these delicious morning options can be prepared ahead for a stress-free start to the day.

items.title: The most viewed photograph in history turns 30. Here's how Bill Gates was involved
items.description: Plastered across screens in offices, schools and homes globally, Bliss is one of the most well-known images in the world.

items.title: Quiz: From an Oscars slap to 'sandpapergate', do you know your history?
items.description: Can you remember who Will Smith slapped, or what happened during "sandpapergate" scandal? Test yourself with today's quiz.

items.title: Queenslanders hit with millions in fines since 50c fares introduced
items.description: The penalties would help authorities recover $7,070.50 in revenue they otherwise would have collected if the commuters had paid their 50 cent fare.

items.title: Drivers say WA's EV highway 'not fit for purpose' amid litany of issues
items.description: Constant malfunctions, long repair times and inadequate power supply are causing some EV drivers to rethink long trips in Western Australia.

items.title: Liberty Bell Bay enters voluntary administration
items.description: The owner of Australia's only manganese alloy smelter has entered voluntary administration. It means further uncertainty for the Tasmanian smelter's workforce.

items.title: French star calls out Danielle Collins for 'BS' claim he slid into her DMs
items.description: Corentin Moutet chides the Tennis Channel after Danielle Collins claimed on-air that he slid into her DMs after she said she did not date "short kings".

items.title: Charge of choking boy dropped against soccer dad after apology
items.description: Perth orthodontist Steven James Naoum walks free from court as a charge alleging he choked an 11-year-old boy at a junior soccer match is dismissed.

items.title: Body found in search for 35yo man who went missing after boat capsized
items.description: Police say a body has been found in the search for a 35-year-old man who went missing after a boating mishap in Tasmania's far north-west at the weekend.

items.title: Concerns health insurers creeping towards US-style managed care
items.description: Increasing partnerships between health insurers, GP centres and telehealth services has raised concerns about a potential two-tier system in which privately insured patients have more affordable access to GP consultations.

items.title: Anglican archbishop apologises to sexual abuse victim
items.description: Beth Heinrich, now 86, was sexually abused as a teenager by Reverend Donald Shearman in the central-west New South Wales town of Forbes in the 1950s where she attended an Anglican-run boarding house.
